p: School holidays and rainy weekends are when indoor parks like this are in highest demand, so booking ahead is the sensible move if you've got a particular day in mind. Midweek in term time is usually calmer, which can suit families with younger children who prefer a bit more space to find their feet.

Dress the kids in comfy clothes with no zips, buckles or sharp bits, leave jewellery at home and tie back long hair. Arriving a few minutes early gets the shoes-and-coats faff out of the way before your time starts. If it's a party, ask about age guidance and group options when you book.

Hertfordshire has some lovely spots for the rest of the day. The Ashridge Estate, looked after by the National Trust near Berkhamsted, has miles of woodland walks and the Bridgewater Monument with views across the Chilterns. Berkhamsted itself has the ruins of a Norman castle right by the railway station, which is free to explore. Further afield, St Albans has its cathedral, Roman remains in Verulamium Park and a busy market. For a family trip with a difference, the Grand Union Canal runs through Hemel's outskirts, with towpath walks and narrowboats to spot. And if you've got Harry Potter fans in tow, the Warner Bros. Studio Tour at Leavesden is only a short drive away, though it needs booking well ahead.
